summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that creates the Medicare Guarantee Fund, which would split into a Treasury and a Health special account.
From 1 July 2017 or later, MBS and PBS payments would be automatically taken from and paid out of the Health special account.

The Treasurer would each year credit the Treasury special account with an amount matching estimated liabilities and transfer that sum to the Health account, with top-up mechanisms to cover shortfalls.
changes: Establishes the Medicare Guarantee Fund with Treasury and Health special accounts.
Automatically debits MBS and PBS payments from the Health special account from 1 July 2017 or later.
Requires the Treasurer to annually credit the Treasury special account with estimated liabilities and transfer that amount to the Health account.
Creates mechanisms to address over and under estimates, including top-ups to the Health account.
summary.affected: The package affects the Department of Health, the Department of the Treasury, and recipients of Medicare and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme payments.

The majority voted against a [motion](http://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2017-06-19.197.1) introduced by Senator [Helen Polley](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/helen_polley) (Tas), which means it failed. The motion asked for this bill to be withdrawn and redrafted *"to provide actual guarantees for the future of Medicare"*. ### What do these bills do? If passed, the [bills](http://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r5900) will create the Medicare Guarantee Fund. The Fund will be used to fund both Medicare benefits and payments under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme [**PBS**]. The creation of this fund is a response to the 2016 election, which the Labor Party accused the Coalition of wanted to privatise Medicare. The [bills digest](http://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd1617a/17bd108) emphasises that these bills don't *"guarantee the continuing existence of Medicare of itself ... speeches.speaker: Scott Morrison
speeches.brief: The MP moved the Medicare Guarantee (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2017, which amends the Health Insurance Act 1973 and National Health Act 1953 to replace existing special appropriations for the MBS and PBS with a Medicare Guarantee Fund, aiming to increase transparency and secure funding for these schemes.

speeches.speaker: Bert Van Manen
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Medicare Guarantee Bill 2017 establishes a Medicare Guarantee Fund to secure ongoing funding for the Medicare Benefits Schedule and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme from 1 July 2017, with an estimated $33.8 billion credited in the next financial year, including $12.1 billion from the Medicare levy.

speeches.speaker: Catherine King
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the Medicare Guarantee Bill is a meaningless accounting trick that does not protect Medicare, citing the government's $2.2 billion freeze on patient rebates, cuts to public hospitals, and only 67% of urgent emergency patients seen within 30 minutes. They proposed amendments to include public hospital funding, immediate indexation of frozen rebates, and reinvestment of savings from the Medicare Benefits Schedule Review.
